title: Identification of the tendon/ligament stem cell in mice and humans.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found GEO series GSE289694 (bulk RNA-seq, 57 samples) and GSE289693 (amplicon lineage tracing, 26 samples) by title search. Downloaded and parsed all three GSE289694 gene-count tables: human 26,475 genes x 24 samples (7 hypertrophic + 5 normal ligamentum flavum donors, 2 sorted populations each), mouse stenosis 24,411 x 21 (7 mice x 3 sorted populations), mouse untreated 24,411 x 12. Opened one amplicon ASV (amplicon sequence variant) table: 2,148 rows x 30 columns.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract; paper is paywalled with no PMC full text, so methods, the full list of datasets and any single-cell data are unknown.

a1_downloadable.note: GEO supplementary count tables download openly (checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Sample condition (hypertrophic vs normal) and sorted cell population are encoded in column names; not a measured per-row outcome but usable as labels.

a3_inputs_present.note: Gene-level salmon counts with Ensembl IDs and gene names present (checked).

a4_units_stated.note: Salmon merged gene counts (read counts), standard nf-core output.

a5_enough_rows.note: 57 bulk RNA-seq samples in total; only 12 human donors and 7-8 mice per experiment. Far under the ~400 needed even for classification. Amplicon lineage data is 26 samples.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO reports 57 samples, matching 24+21+12 columns in the files; paper counts not checked (paywalled).

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are clinical diagnosis and FACS (fluorescence-activated cell sorting) gate, physical measurements.

honest_claim_h3: With 12 human donors, a model could at most claim to separate hypertrophic from normal ligamentum flavum sorted-cell transcriptomes in this one cohort.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gene expression of sorted ligament cells to predict whether the ligament came from a spinal stenosis patient.
plain_idea.train_on: Bulk gene counts for ~26,000 genes per sorted cell population; 24 human samples from 12 donors (verified).
plain_idea.predict: Hypertrophic (stenosis) versus normal ligament, from clinical diagnosis at surgery.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would hint at a stenosis expression signature, but 12 donors cannot support a trustworthy model; a differential expression analysis already answers this.

ml_idea: Classify hypertrophic vs normal ligamentum flavum from sorted-cell bulk RNA-seq; not viable at 57 samples.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from downloaded file sizes; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count samples in GEO: 57 bulk samples, 12 human donors — already kills it.

verdict_reason: Fails A5: the public data is 57 bulk RNA-seq samples of sorted cells (12 human donors, ~15 mice) plus 26 lineage amplicon samples, verified in GEO files; far too few for ML.
